email.body1:
Jamie, saw Ethena raised a $30M Series B and is expanding into Code of Conduct and Data Privacy training.

Scaling that fast usually means more accounts in play than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

Given your GTM engineering focus, I built a personalized signal play for Ethena off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Jamie, quick follow-up for Ethena.

Post-raise, expectations on pipeline usually jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Ethena needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Jamie, last bit of proof for Ethena.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Ethena's reply rate likely compares to other Series-B compliance-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jamie, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything right after a raise, and the fundraise-to-hiring stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a GTM-engineering motion? I'll tailor it to Ethena either way.
